text:
Simon Nemec signed a five-year contract with Calgary on Nov. 5 at $7.25 million a year, per Flames Nation. That's a big bet on a 22-year-old who arrived from New Jersey and has yet to score in 17 games with the Flames. The bet makes more sense than the goal column does.

He has 2.57 expected goals on 29 shots, so a 0 for the season is bad luck rather than bad shooting, and Calgary has scored 5.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. He plays 21 minutes a night, and Kevin Bahl's season-ending injury will push that higher.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows why the Flames paid. He stops 18% of the entries aimed at him (typical is 11%), carries the puck in on almost half his entries, and gets shots off passes across the slot. His top speed ranks in the 91st percentile. The concern is that Calgary takes only 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five. As the second overall pick in 2022, between Juraj Slafkovsky and Logan Cooley, the expectations were always going to be big. We project about 32 points.
headline: Nemec got paid. Now the goals.
